a1341444-42ec-4bd0-9d97-93a605dd33a2.text: Some people will tell you to take malic and citric acid (which make green apples and tart cherries sour) as an extra quick energy source for your enterocytes. And they do supply quick energy, because they are made and used by that mitochondrial energy cycle, also called the TCA or Krebs cycle. But glutamine is still the main thing they need, because it helps build new cells in addition to giving the needed energy. Those acids do help you absorb iron, though. In one study, people absorbed two to three times as much of the iron in a rice meal when 1 g of pure malic or citric acid was mixed in (Gillooly et al., 1983), probably because the acids help keep the iron dissolved so the gut can take it up. So something sour with an iron-rich meal is worth having anyway.
